newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas still mostly down late on cash, temps.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas still mostly down late on cash, temps.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mostly lower late Monday in thin trade, undermined by follow-through technical selling and forecasts for fairly mild eastern weather this week which has pressured the cash.
At 1345 EDT, June slipped 0.3 cent to $2.239 per million British thermal units, while July was 0.7 cent lower at $2.24. Most other deferreds were down by 0.3 to 2.5 cents.

"Early last week we went up a little too fast, but it was more technical than fundamental, and the forecast this week doesn't promise a lot of demand," said one trader, noting some technical follow through after the selloff late last week.
Maintenance work on Transco's Texas line, which began Saturday, will cut the line's total capacity of about 600 mmcfd from May 14-19, with 400 mmcfd still cut from May 20-22.
While injections are likely to pick up and help support physical prices near-term, few expected much upside until broader cooling loads kick in, perhaps later in the month.

Temperatures this week in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic were expected to range around normal, with the milder weather coming later in the week. The Southeast starts the week below-normal, then warms to near-normal. The Midwest is expected to stay below-normal all week but moderate somewhat by the weekend. In the Southwest, above-normal temperatures are expected to continue.

Technically, traders pegged important support in June in the $2.195-2.20 area, with sell stops likely below that number. Major buying was likely at $2.05, which is a double bottom and coincides this week with key trendline support. Resistance was seen at the contract high of $2.43 and then at $2.47-50.
In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices slipped a few cents to the low-to-mid $2.20s. Midcon pipes were down slightly to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas also was modestly lower in the low-$2.50s.
NYMEX said 17,285 contracts traded at 1305 EDT.
On the KCBT, June edged up one cent to $2.10, while deferreds were steady to down 1.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.3 cents to 13.9 cents (NYMEX premium).
